_comment: Clarifications shown under a problem's statement, added 2026-09-24.
LeetCode's statements are shown verbatim and are never edited here. But LeetCode has dropped
the definitions it used to carry — 'A subarray is a contiguous non-empty sequence...' — and
several statements now use their central term without ever defining it. Longest Consecutive
Sequence never says what a consecutive sequence is, so it reads as though the run has to be
adjacent in the array. NeetCode's rewrites define these terms; these notes say the same thing,
in the app's own words, without touching the statement itself.
Add a slug here when a statement leaves its own term undefined. Keep it to definitions: a hint
about how to solve the problem does not belong on the page that sets it.

longest-consecutive-sequence: A consecutive sequence is a sequence of elements in which each element is exactly 1 greater than the previous element. The elements do not have to be next to each other in the original array.
maximum-subarray: A subarray is a contiguous, non-empty run of elements within the array.
maximum-product-subarray: A subarray is a contiguous, non-empty run of elements within the array.
longest-substring-without-repeating-char: A substring is a contiguous run of characters within the string.
A subsequence keeps the order but may skip characters, so it is not the same thing: in "pwwkew", "pwke" is a subsequence but not a substring.
longest-repeating-character-replacement: A substring is a contiguous run of characters within the string.
permutation-in-string: A substring is a contiguous run of characters within the string.
minimum-window-substring: A substring is a contiguous run of characters within the string.
longest-palindromic-substring: A substring is a contiguous run of characters within the string.
palindrome-partitioning: A substring is a contiguous run of characters within the string, so the parts of a partition are the pieces s is cut into, in order.
interleaving-string: A substring is a contiguous run of characters within the string.
longest-increasing-subsequence: A subsequence is what is left after deleting some elements (possibly none) without reordering the rest, so its elements do not have to be next to each other in the array.
Strictly increasing means each element is greater than the one before it; equal neighbours do not count.
distinct-subsequences: A subsequence is what is left after deleting some characters (possibly none) without reordering the rest, so its characters do not have to be next to each other in the string.
hand-of-straights: Consecutive cards means their values increase by exactly 1 each time, such as 2, 3, 4. Order in the hand does not matter, since the cards are rearranged.
